projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
Analytics dashboard project covering three major workstreams: (1) customer CSV data processing and ingestion, (2) application log analysis, and (3) visualization components and dashboard UI. Goal: deliver a unified analytics dashboard that ingests customer CSV data and application logs, transforms and validates them, and surfaces insights through interactive visualizations.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-processing, log-analysis, visualization

tasks.name: Milestone 1: Foundation, Architecture & Data Contracts
tasks.details:
Establish the technical foundation before any pipeline code is written: technology choices, repository/dev environment, storage layer, and — most importantly — the data contracts (schemas) that the CSV pipeline, the log pipeline, and the visualization layer all agree on. Getting schemas fixed early prevents rework in three downstream workstreams.

Exit criteria: documented architecture decision records, runnable dev environment, storage provisioned, versioned schema definitions committed and reviewed.

tasks.name: Milestone 2: Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing Pipeline
tasks.details:
Build the end-to-end pipeline that takes raw customer CSV files and turns them into validated, cleaned, deduplicated, analytics-ready tables. Covers file intake, schema validation, cleaning, quarantine of bad rows, transformation into aggregation-friendly models, and idempotent loading.

Exit criteria: pipeline runs end-to-end on representative production-shaped CSVs, handles malformed input without crashing, is covered by unit/integration tests, and writes to the agreed storage layer.

tasks.name: Milestone 3: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Build the pipeline that parses application logs from multiple formats, normalizes timestamps and severity levels, correlates related events, and produces the operational aggregates the dashboard needs (error rates, latency percentiles, top failing endpoints, volume over time).

Exit criteria: parser handles all log formats observed in production, aggregates are queryable and verified against hand-computed expectations, and the pipeline runs reliably on large daily log volumes.

tasks.name: Milestone 4: Visualization Components & Dashboard UI
tasks.details:
Build the dashboard front end: layout shell, reusable chart primitives, the customer analytics views, the operational/log views, and the filtering and data-fetching layer that connects the UI to the processed data.

Exit criteria: all planned views render real processed data, shared chart components are reused across views, filters work consistently, and the UI meets accessibility and responsiveness baselines.

tasks.name: Milestone 5: Integration, Testing & Hardening
tasks.details:
Wire the pipelines to the UI through a stable query/API surface, then harden the whole system: end-to-end tests, performance validation on realistic data volumes, PII/security review of customer data handling, and observability.

Exit criteria: end-to-end test suite passes in CI, dashboard meets latency targets at target data volume, PII handling reviewed and signed off, alerts and dashboards-on-dashboard (pipeline health) in place.

tasks.name: Milestone 6: Deployment, Documentation & Launch
tasks.details:
Ship it: production deployment of pipelines and front end, scheduled orchestration, runbooks, user-facing documentation, and a staged rollout.

Exit criteria: production deployment is automated and repeatable, on-call runbook exists, documentation is published, and the first real users have access.

tasks.name: Select tech stack and record architecture decisions
tasks.details:
Choose and document: data processing runtime (e.g. Python + pandas/Polars vs. dbt/SQL), storage/warehouse, query API layer, frontend framework and charting library. Produce a short ADR for each irreversible choice, including why the alternative was rejected.

Deliverable: 4-6 one-page ADRs in docs/adr/ covering runtime, storage, API, frontend.

tasks.name: Scaffold repository, dev environment and CI skeleton
tasks.details:
Create monorepo layout (pipelines/, api/, dashboard/, infra/), dependency manifests and lockfiles, Makefile/justfile targets for setup/test/lint, pre-commit hooks (formatter + linter), and a CI workflow that runs lint + unit tests on every PR. Add a short CONTRIBUTING note with local setup steps.

Deliverable: fresh clone can run `make setup && make test` successfully; CI is green on the initial commit.

tasks.name: Provision storage layer and dev/staging environments
tasks.details:
Stand up the chosen storage (warehouse/schema or object store + query engine) with separate dev and staging environments. Create the database/schema namespaces for raw, staged, and analytics layers (raw_customer, raw_logs, stg_*, mart_*). Add connection config via environment variables and a local docker-compose equivalent so developers can run the stack offline.

Deliverable: documented connection setup, committed schema/layer definitions, local stack boots from docker-compose.

tasks.name: Define customer data schema and contracts
tasks.details:
Inventory the real customer CSV files: columns, dtypes, encodings, delimiters, null conventions, and known dirty-data patterns. Then write versioned schema definitions for raw_customer and the downstream stg_customer / dim_customer / fct_customer_daily models, including primary keys, required vs. optional fields, allowed enum values, and the uniqueness grain of each table.

Deliverable: schema file(s) in the repo + a documented field dictionary reviewed by whoever owns the customer data.

tasks.name: Define log event schema and contracts
tasks.details:
Collect a sample of every application log format in use (structured JSON, key=value, plaintext with regex-extractable fields). Define the canonical normalized log event schema (event_id, timestamp_utc, severity, service, endpoint/route, status_code, latency_ms, trace_id, user_id_masked, message, error_type) plus the aggregate marts the dashboard will read.

Deliverable: normalized log event schema + field dictionary + samples of each source format committed as fixtures.

tasks.name: Classify PII in customer and log data and set handling rules
tasks.details:
Enumerate which fields are PII (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, IPs, user IDs in logs). Decide per field: retain, hash/tokenize, truncate, or drop before it reaches the analytics layer or the dashboard UI. Document masking rules and where they must be applied (ingest vs. query vs. render) so the same rule isn't implemented three different ways later.

Deliverable: PII field classification table + masking rules doc; downstream tasks reference it rather than re-deciding.

tasks.name: Build CSV file intake and reader
tasks.details:
Implement discovery and reading of incoming customer CSV files from the agreed drop location (local dir now, object store later), with encoding detection (UTF-8/UTF-8-BOM/Latin-1), delimiter and quoting sniffing, header normalization, chunked/streaming reads for large files, and idempotent file bookkeeping (record file name, size, checksum, ingest time so the same file isn't double-processed).

Deliverable: reader module + unit tests on at least 3 differently-formatted sample files, including one >100MB file to prove streaming works.

tasks.name: Implement schema validation and type coercion
tasks.details:
Validate each row against the customer data contract: required columns present, no unexpected/missing headers, dtype coercion (dates in multiple formats, decimals, integers, booleans), enum membership checks, and range/business-rule checks (e.g. non-negative revenue, signup_date <= today). Produce a structured validation report (per-column error counts) rather than a single exception.

Deliverable: validator module, machine-readable validation report, tests covering each failure class.

tasks.name: Implement data cleaning and normalization
tasks.details:
Normalize values so downstream aggregation is trustworthy: canonicalize emails (lowercase/trim), phone numbers (E.164), country/region names, and currency; standardize null representations; trim whitespace; detect and resolve duplicate customer records using the agreed business key (e.g. customer_id, falling back to normalized email), recording which duplicate won and why.

Deliverable: cleaning module with explicit, documented rules; duplicate-resolution report written per run; tests with dirty-sample fixtures.

tasks.name: Add malformed-row quarantine and error reporting
tasks.details:
Rows that fail validation must not abort the run and must not silently disappear. Route them to a quarantine table/store with the source file, row number, raw line, failing rule, and error message. Emit a run summary (rows read / accepted / quarantined, per-rule counts) and make quarantine contents queryable so the data owner can fix the source file.

Deliverable: quarantine path implemented end-to-end; deliberately corrupt fixture produces the expected quarantine rows and summary.

tasks.name: Transform cleaned data into analytics-ready models
tasks.details:
Build the dimensional models the dashboard will query: dim_customer (one row per customer, current attributes), fct_customer_daily (daily grain activity/revenue snapshots), and segment/cohort support tables. Apply the masking rules from the PII task before data lands in the mart layer. Document the grain of every table and validate uniqueness on the declared keys.

Deliverable: mart models + grain documentation + uniqueness tests passing on real-shaped data.

tasks.name: Implement idempotent incremental loading with watermarks
tasks.details:
Make reruns safe: upsert/merge on declared keys instead of blind append, track a per-source watermark (last processed file checksum + max updated_at), support backfills for a date range without duplicating rows, and fail loudly if the target grain would be violated. Add a small CLI to run full vs. incremental loads.

Deliverable: rerunning the same batch twice produces zero duplicate rows (proven by a test); backfill command works for a 30-day window.

tasks.name: Build CSV test fixtures and pipeline test suite
tasks.details:
Assemble a fixture library of realistic customer CSVs: happy path, missing columns, wrong dtypes, duplicate keys, mixed encodings, embedded commas/newlines in quoted fields, unicode names, empty file, and a large synthetic file for performance. Write unit tests per stage plus one integration test that runs the whole pipeline from file to mart and asserts row counts and key aggregates.

Deliverable: fixtures committed under tests/fixtures/ with a README; integration test runs in CI in under a few minutes.

tasks.name: Build multi-format log parser
tasks.details:
Implement per-format parsers behind a common interface: structured JSON lines, key=value pairs, and plaintext with named regex patterns. Auto-detect the format per file/source with an explicit override, handle multi-line stack traces by attaching them to the originating event, and never drop an unparseable line — emit it as a raw fallback record with the parse error.

Deliverable: parser package with one module per format, detection logic, and unit tests on golden samples of each format.

tasks.name: Normalize timestamps, timezones and severity levels
tasks.details:
Convert all event timestamps to UTC while retaining the original offset, parse the several timestamp formats found in practice (ISO-8601, epoch seconds/ms, Apache-style), and map source severity vocabulary (WARN/WARNING/ERR/CRITICAL/5/ERROR) onto the canonical enum. Flag events with unparseable or implausible timestamps (e.g. far in the future) into the quarantine stream rather than guessing.

Deliverable: normalization module + table of source-to-canonical severity mappings + tests including DST-boundary and epoch-unit confusion cases.

tasks.name: Extract service, endpoint and error-type dimensions
tasks.details:
Derive the dimensions the dashboard groups by: service name, HTTP route/endpoint (normalized so /orders/123 and /orders/456 collapse to /orders/{id}), status code class, and error type (exception class or normalized message signature). Add light clustering of high-cardinality free-text error messages into stable signatures so "top errors" is actually readable.

Deliverable: enrichment module + tests proving route templating and message signature clustering produce stable, bounded cardinality.

tasks.name: Correlate events by trace ID and build sessions
tasks.details:
Group events sharing a trace_id/request_id into request-level records spanning services, then derive user sessions with a defined inactivity timeout. Handle out-of-order and late-arriving events (allowed lateness window), orphan events with no parent, and duplicated events shipped twice by the log agent. Emit per-request records (entry service, total duration, services touched, terminal status, error flag).

Deliverable: correlation module + docs on the lateness window and session timeout; tests for out-of-order, orphan, and duplicate events.

tasks.name: Build operational aggregates mart for logs
tasks.details:
Produce the time-bucketed aggregates the dashboard reads: event volume and error count/rate per bucket, latency p50/p95/p99 per endpoint and service, top-N failing endpoints and error signatures, and status-code-class distribution. Support 1-minute, 1-hour and 1-day grains so the UI can switch resolution without rescanning raw logs. Handle sparse buckets (emit zero-filled or null explicitly — pick one and document it).

Deliverable: aggregate tables + documented grain/fill semantics + reconciliation test comparing one bucket against a hand-computed value from raw events.

tasks.name: Define log retention and rollup strategy
tasks.details:
Decide how long raw events are kept vs. how long aggregates are kept, and implement the rollup/expiry job (e.g. raw 30 days -> hourly 1 year -> daily indefinitely). Confirm the dashboard's max selectable time range is fully answerable from retained aggregates, and document the cost/retention trade-off.

Deliverable: retention policy doc + working expiry/rollup job with a dry-run mode and a test proving expired raw data still leaves intact aggregates.

tasks.name: Build log parser golden-sample fixtures and test suite
tasks.details:
Collect golden samples of each real log format (including ugly cases: stack traces, truncated lines, nested JSON, unicode, very long messages, missing fields) and write tests asserting parsed field-by-field output. Add a regression test that fails loudly if a format change silently breaks parsing (parse success rate drops below a threshold).

Deliverable: fixtures + golden-output tests + parse-success-rate guard in CI.

tasks.name: Define dashboard information architecture and view specs
tasks.details:
Agree the page structure and, for each view, write a one-page spec: question it answers, metrics shown, dimensions/filters, chart type, empty/loading/error behavior, and drill-down target. Cover at minimum: customer overview, customer segments/cohorts, revenue or activity trend, operational health (error rate, latency), and error/endpoint drill-down. Validate the specs against the fields actually produced by the pipelines so no view depends on data that doesn't exist.

Deliverable: IA doc + per-view specs reviewed with stakeholders; explicit list of any metric that requires new pipeline work.

tasks.name: Build app shell: routing, layout, navigation and theming
tasks.details:
Stand up the frontend skeleton: route structure matching the IA, page layout with header/sidebar/content regions, design tokens (spacing, type scale, color palette with accessible contrast), dark/light support if in scope, and a 404/error boundary. Include a Storybook or equivalent harness so components can be developed in isolation.

Deliverable: routes render placeholder pages; tokens and base components documented in Storybook; lighthouse/a11y baseline clean on the shell.

tasks.name: Build reusable chart component library
tasks.details:
Wrap the chosen charting library in a small set of opinionated, accessible components: KPI/stat card, time-series line/area, bar (incl. stacked), horizontal ranked bar, data table with sorting, and sparkline. Each takes a typed data prop and handles its own empty/loading/error state. Keep formatting (numbers, currency, percentages, dates) in shared utilities rather than duplicated per chart.

Deliverable: component library with Storybook stories per component covering empty, single-point, dense, and long-label data; unit tests for the formatting utilities.

tasks.name: Build data fetching layer with caching and state handling
tasks.details:
Implement the client data layer: typed API client generated from or checked against the API contract, query hooks with caching, request de-duplication, retry with backoff, cancellation on filter change, and consistent loading/skeleton/empty/error UI states. Handle partial failure (one widget fails, the page still renders) and stale-while-revalidate so filter changes feel instant.

Deliverable: data layer + a documented pattern that every view uses; tests with mocked API covering success, empty, slow, and error responses.

tasks.name: Build customer analytics views
tasks.details:
Assemble the customer-facing pages from the chart library + data layer: customer overview KPIs (total, new, active, churned), segment breakdown, cohort retention table/heatmap, and activity or revenue trend with comparison period. Each view must state its denominator and time grain on screen so numbers can't be misread.

Deliverable: views rendering real pipeline data, with per-view acceptance checks against the spec and a manual number sanity check vs. a direct query.

tasks.name: Build operational health and log analysis views
tasks.details:
Assemble the operational pages: error rate over time, request volume, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) with a selectable service/endpoint, top failing endpoints, top error signatures, and a drill-down table of recent events for a selected bucket. Rendering of user identifiers in log drill-downs must follow the PII masking rules.

Deliverable: views rendering real aggregate data with time-grain switching (1m/1h/1d) verified to change resolution correctly; drill-down reaches raw events where retention allows.

tasks.name: Implement global filters, date range and URL state
tasks.details:
One filter bar driving all views: date range with presets plus custom range, service/environment selector for log views, customer segment selector for customer views, and cross-filtering where a chart click narrows the page. Persist filter state in the URL so a view can be shared or bookmarked, and keep state consistent when navigating between pages.

Deliverable: filter state encoded in URL, shareable deep links reproduce the exact view; tests for preset ranges, invalid URL params, and cross-filter behavior.

tasks.name: Complete accessibility and responsive layout pass
tasks.details:
Sweep every view for accessibility: keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic landmarks, chart alternatives (data table or text summary for screen readers), sufficient color contrast for chart series that survives color-blindness, and reduced-motion support. Then make layouts responsive from desktop down to tablet and a usable narrow-mobile fallback (tables scroll or collapse to cards).

Deliverable: automated a11y checks in CI (axe or equivalent) with zero violations, manual keyboard-only walkthrough notes, and screenshots at 3 breakpoints.

tasks.name: Optimize frontend rendering for large datasets
tasks.details:
Apply downsampling/LTTB for long time series, virtualization for long tables, memoized selectors to avoid recompute on filter change, route-level code splitting, and chart re-render throttling on resize. Measure before/after with a profiling run on a realistic large dataset and record the numbers.

Deliverable: documented budget (e.g. initial JS size, time-to-interactive, interaction latency at 1M-point aggregate volume) with measurements showing the targets are met.

tasks.name: Build query API over the analytics marts
tasks.details:
Expose the marts through a small read-only API: endpoints for each view's data needs (customer KPIs, segments, cohort matrix, time series, aggregate buckets, drill-down rows), with validated query params (date range bounds, grain, filters, pagination) and hard limits so no request can table-scan the world. Include query caching and a response schema version. Publish an OpenAPI/typed contract that the frontend consumes.

Deliverable: API with contract tests, request validation, pagination, and per-endpoint latency measured at realistic volume.

tasks.name: Write end-to-end test suite across pipeline and UI
tasks.details:
Build an E2E suite that seeds fixtures, runs both pipelines, serves the API, and asserts the dashboard shows the expected numbers: KPI values match a direct mart query, filters change results correctly, time-grain switching works, and empty/error states render. Keep the seeded dataset small enough to run in CI but shaped like production.

Deliverable: E2E suite green in CI with deterministic fixtures; failure messages identify which metric diverged and by how much.

tasks.name: Run performance and load testing at target data volume
tasks.details:
Generate production-scale synthetic data (target row counts and daily log volume), then measure pipeline runtime, memory, API p95 latency per endpoint, and dashboard interaction latency. Identify the top bottleneck, fix it if cheap, otherwise file a follow-up with numbers. Record the results as a benchmark baseline to detect regressions.

Deliverable: benchmark report with pass/fail against agreed SLOs and a committed baseline for future comparison.

tasks.name: Conduct security and PII compliance review
tasks.details:
Verify the PII rules from Milestone 1 are actually enforced end to end: no raw PII in mart tables or API responses, no PII leaked into logs of the dashboard itself or error messages, secrets only via env/secret manager (none in git), least-privilege DB roles (read-only for API), and transport encryption. Add an automated test that scans mart schemas/API payloads for known PII column patterns so this can't silently regress.

Deliverable: signed-off review checklist + automated PII-leak test in CI + list of accepted residual risks.

tasks.name: Add observability: pipeline health, freshness and alerting
tasks.details:
Emit structured run metrics for each pipeline run (status, rows in/out/quarantined, duration, watermark), plus data-freshness signals per mart. Add alert rules for: pipeline failure, unexpected quarantine-rate spike, freshness lag beyond threshold, and parse-success-rate drop. Build a small internal health page or dashboard panel so the on-call person sees pipeline state without reading logs.

Deliverable: metrics emitted, alert rules committed as code, health panel live in staging, one deliberately triggered alert demonstrated.

tasks.name: Add automated data quality checks and reconciliation
tasks.details:
Define data quality assertions per mart — uniqueness on keys, referential integrity (fct rows resolve to a dim row), not-null on required fields, row-count deltas vs. previous run within bounds, and aggregate reconciliation (daily totals equal the sum of their buckets). Fail the run or warn per severity, and record results in a quality log visible over time.

Deliverable: quality check suite running after every pipeline run with a documented severity policy; deliberately broken fixture is caught by the checks.

tasks.name: Set up infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD deployment
tasks.details:
Codify the environments (storage, API service, frontend hosting, scheduler) as IaC so staging and production are reproducible. Build a CI/CD pipeline: test -> build artifacts -> deploy staging automatically -> promote to production on approval, with a documented one-command rollback. Separate credentials per environment.

Deliverable: `terraform plan` (or equivalent) clean with no drift, staging deploy automated, production deploy gated and rehearsed once end to end.

tasks.name: Configure pipeline orchestration and scheduling
tasks.details:
Schedule the CSV and log pipelines on the agreed cadence, with retries and backoff on failure, concurrency guards so two runs can't overlap on the same target, dependency ordering (customer dim before daily fact; log rollup after aggregates), and alerting on repeated failure. Include a manual trigger path for backfills.

Deliverable: scheduled jobs running in staging for a week without manual intervention; overlap guard proven by a test of concurrent triggers.

tasks.name: Write operational runbooks and on-call guidance
tasks.details:
Document the failure modes people will actually hit and exactly what to do: pipeline failed mid-run, quarantine rate spike, stale data on the dashboard, wrong numbers reported by a user, API down, rollback procedure, and how to backfill a date range. Include where logs and metrics live, expected run durations, and who owns each component.

Deliverable: runbook with a section per failure mode, each with detection signal, first checks, and remediation; validated by someone not on the build team following it in a game-day drill.

tasks.name: Publish user and developer documentation
tasks.details:
Write two docs: (1) a user guide defining every metric and dimension on the dashboard — numerator, denominator, grain, and known caveats, so nobody misreads a chart; (2) a developer guide covering local setup, architecture overview, how to add a new metric end to end (pipeline -> mart -> API -> chart), and the data contracts. Keep both in the repo so they version with the code.

Deliverable: metric dictionary covering 100% of displayed metrics, developer guide with a worked "add a metric" walkthrough, both linked from the README.

tasks.name: Execute staged rollout and launch
tasks.details:
Roll out in stages: internal team only -> a small pilot group of real users -> general availability. For each stage define the success signals (usage, no data incidents, no number-escalations, latency within SLO), the rollback trigger, and a feedback capture mechanism. Run a short retrospective after the pilot stage and fold fixes in before GA.

Deliverable: launch checklist completed per stage, pilot feedback summarized with actions, GA announcement sent.

tasks.name: Build dim_customer model
tasks.details:
One row per customer with current attributes only (latest-wins merge across source files). Implement the merge order rule, keep a stable surrogate key plus the natural key, and add uniqueness tests on both. Exclude or mask PII columns per the classification table.

Deliverable: dim_customer built by the pipeline with uniqueness tests passing and a documented precedence rule for conflicting records.

tasks.name: Build fct_customer_daily fact model
tasks.details:
Daily-grain fact table keyed by (date, customer_key) holding activity and revenue metrics. Define exactly how a customer's daily value is derived from sparse source data (carry-forward vs. zero — pick one and write it down), handle late-arriving days by rewriting affected partitions, and assert one row per (date, customer) in a test.

Deliverable: fact model + documented sparse-day semantics + partition-rewrite support proven by a backfill test.

tasks.name: Build segment and cohort support models
tasks.details:
Materialize the aggregates the dashboard's segment breakdown and cohort retention views need: customer counts by segment over time, and a cohort matrix (signup month x months since signup, with retained counts and the denominator made explicit). Validate against a small hand-computed example.

Deliverable: cohort/segment models + a hand-checked test fixture whose expected matrix is written out longhand.

tasks.name: Apply PII masking in the mart layer
tasks.details:
Implement the masking transformations defined in the PII classification task at the point data enters the marts: hash/tokenize identifiers, truncate or drop free-text PII, and keep a keyed alias column where the UI needs to show a stable pseudonymous identifier. Add a test that fails if a raw PII column ever appears in a mart schema.

Deliverable: masking implemented once in a shared module used by all mart builds, with the schema-guard test in CI.

tasks.name: Assemble request records from trace IDs
tasks.details:
Group events by trace_id into one request record: entry service, entry timestamp, terminal status, total duration, and the list of services touched. Handle traces that never terminate (timeout after the lateness window) by marking them incomplete rather than dropping them.

Deliverable: request-assembly step producing one record per trace, with tests for complete, incomplete, and single-event traces.

tasks.name: Derive user sessions with inactivity timeout
tasks.details:
Group a pseudonymous user's requests into sessions using a configurable inactivity gap, emit session records (start, end, duration, request count, error count, entry and exit endpoints), and make the timeout a documented parameter rather than a hardcoded constant. Test the exact boundary: one millisecond either side of the timeout.

Deliverable: sessionization step + boundary test + doc explaining how timeout choice affects reported session counts.

tasks.name: Handle late-arriving, duplicate and orphan events
tasks.details:
Implement the allowed-lateness window and define what happens to events older than it (route to a late bucket vs. drop with a counter), deduplicate events shipped twice by the log agent using the event fingerprint, and surface orphan events (no matching trace) as a countable category instead of silently merging them into requests.

Deliverable: explicit handling for all three cases with counters emitted per run and tests for each; no event is silently lost without a metric.

tasks.name: Build error rate and volume aggregates
tasks.details:
Time-bucketed counts of total events, error events, and derived error rate, sliced by service and severity. Make the error-rate denominator explicit (errors / all events vs. errors / requests) and implement whichever the spec chose, documented in the column description.

Deliverable: aggregate table + column-level descriptions stating numerator and denominator; test asserting rate = errors/total for a known fixture.

tasks.name: Build latency percentile aggregates
tasks.details:
Compute p50/p95/p99 latency per endpoint, service and time bucket using an appropriate method (exact for small volumes, t-digest/histogram when volume requires it), and document which method is used so the numbers are reproducible. Exclude requests with no measurable duration rather than treating them as zero.

Deliverable: percentile aggregates + a test comparing computed percentiles against a brute-force calculation on a fixture; method choice documented.

tasks.name: Build top-N rankings and status code distribution
tasks.details:
Produce top-N failing endpoints and top-N error signatures per bucket, plus status-code-class distribution (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx). Define tie-breaking so the ranking is stable between runs, cap N at a sensible value, and make sure "other" is not silently dropped — report the remainder share.

Deliverable: ranking tables + stable tie-break rule documented + test proving identical output across two runs on the same input.

tasks.name: Define grain and fill semantics with reconciliation tests
tasks.details:
Decide and document what a bucket means (UTC-aligned, half-open interval), how empty buckets are represented (zero-filled vs. null), and how the three grains relate (hourly must sum to daily). Then write reconciliation tests: hourly-to-daily rollup equality, totals preserved across grain switches, and one bucket checked against a hand-computed value from raw events.

Deliverable: documented bucket semantics + reconciliation test suite passing on fixture data.

tasks.name: Build KPI stat card and shared formatting utilities
tasks.details:
Implement the KPI/stat card component (value, label, optional delta vs. comparison period with direction-aware color and an icon, not color alone) plus shared formatters for numbers, currency, percentages, compact notation and dates. Formatters must be locale-aware and unit-tested — no ad-hoc formatting inside components.

Deliverable: KpiCard component with empty/loading/error stories; formatter unit tests covering negatives, zero, large numbers, and locale variants.

tasks.name: Build time-series line and area chart component
tasks.details:
Implement the main time-series chart: configurable series, shared tooltip across series, gap handling for missing buckets (gap, not a misleading straight line), y-axis zero baseline policy, and a threshold/annotation band for SLO lines. Include the accessible data-table alternative behind a toggle.

Deliverable: LineChart/AreaChart component with stories for single series, multi-series, sparse data, single point, and very long ranges.

tasks.name: Build bar, stacked bar and ranked bar components
tasks.details:
Implement vertical bar, stacked bar (for status-code-class composition) and horizontal ranked bar (for top-N endpoints and error signatures). Handle long category labels via truncation with full text on hover/focus, sorted order, and a visible "other" segment when the remainder is aggregated.

Deliverable: three bar components with stories covering long labels, many categories, zero-value segments, and the aggregated-remainder case.

tasks.name: Build sortable data table component
tasks.details:
Implement the table used for drill-downs and cohort matrices: column sorting, sticky header, numeric right-alignment, configurable cell renderers, pagination or virtualized scrolling for long lists, and keyboard-accessible sorting. Expose a compact mode for embedding under charts.

Deliverable: DataTable component with stories for wide tables, long lists, empty state, and a cohort-matrix heatmap variant.

tasks.name: Add sparkline component and finalize component docs
tasks.details:
Implement the compact sparkline used inside stat cards and tables, then finish the component library documentation: a README per component with props table, do/don't usage notes, and a short "which chart for which question" decision guide so view builders pick consistently.

Deliverable: Sparkline with stories + complete component docs; the decision guide reviewed with whoever builds the views.

tasks.name: Provision warehouse and create raw/staged/mart schema layers
tasks.details:
Create the dev and staging environments in the chosen warehouse, then define the three logical layers with their namespaces: raw_* (append-only landing), stg_* (cleaned/typed), mart_* (analytics-ready). Encode layer definitions as committed files so they can be recreated. Configure least-privilege roles: loader role for pipelines (write to raw/stg), read-only role for the API.

Deliverable: environments reachable, schema layers created, role grants documented, and the definitions committed to the repo.

tasks.name: Stand up local docker-compose stack for offline development
tasks.details:
Provide a local equivalent of the stack (database/query engine plus any storage emulator) via docker-compose so developers can run pipelines and the API without cloud access. Wire connection settings through environment variables with a committed .env.example, and document the one-command start.

Deliverable: `docker compose up` yields a working local stack; a developer with no cloud credentials can run the pipeline test suite against it.

tasks.name: Build typed API client with caching and query hooks
tasks.details:
Generate or hand-write a typed client from the published API contract, then wrap it in query hooks that provide caching, request de-duplication, retry with backoff, and cancellation when filters change. Keep cache keys derived from the filter state so identical views share cache entries.

Deliverable: typed client + hooks with tests asserting de-duplication (one network call for concurrent identical queries) and cancellation on filter change.

tasks.name: Implement loading, empty, error and partial-failure UI states
tasks.details:
Define one shared pattern for widget states: loading skeleton sized like the real chart to avoid layout shift, explicit empty state ("no data in this range") distinct from zero values, per-widget error with retry, and partial failure so one broken widget cannot blank the page. Document the pattern once and have every view use it.

Deliverable: shared state components + tests for slow, empty, and error responses; a page with one failing widget demonstrably still renders the rest.

tasks.name: Emit pipeline run metrics and data freshness signals
tasks.details:
Emit structured metrics per pipeline run: status, duration, rows read/accepted/quarantined, bytes processed, watermark value, and per-rule error counts. Also publish a freshness timestamp per mart table so consumers can tell how stale the data is without querying the data itself.

Deliverable: metrics visible in the monitoring system with a documented metric-name contract; freshness value correct after a run and unchanged when a run is skipped.

tasks.name: Define alert rules and build pipeline health panel
tasks.details:
Codify alert rules as configuration: pipeline failure, freshness lag past threshold, quarantine-rate spike beyond a baseline band, and parse-success-rate drop. Tune thresholds against a week of staging behaviour to avoid constant noise, and build a single health panel showing per-pipeline last-run status, freshness, and key counts.

Deliverable: alert rules committed as code, health panel live in staging, and one alert demonstrated firing and resolving.

tasks.name: Write mart data quality assertion suite
tasks.details:
Implement the assertions themselves: uniqueness on declared keys, referential integrity from fct to dim, not-null on required fields, row-count delta bounds versus the previous run, and aggregate reconciliation (daily total equals sum of its hourly buckets). Run them after every pipeline load.

Deliverable: assertion suite wired into the load, with a report listing each check, its result, and the failing row sample when it fails.

tasks.name: Add quality severity policy and quality log reporting
tasks.details:
Classify each check as blocking (fail the run, don't publish) or warning (publish but alert), document the reasoning, and persist results to a quality log table so trends are visible over time. Add a deliberately broken fixture proving a blocking check halts publication while a warning check does not.

Deliverable: severity policy doc + quality log + two tests demonstrating blocking vs. warning behaviour.
